instructions: Fresh review of each primary candidate: read dialogue first, then exact cards. Assess all six unchanged criteria and all coach-2.0 gates with turn-specific evidence. For pairs, show whether the Stance changes HOW A pursues the Drive in one interaction. Do not invent missing backstory or assume prior approval. Use the alternate only to assess meaningful differentiation. Report actual reservations. No writer scores or improvement claims are supplied.
productionStandard:
PRODUCTION STANDARD coach-2.0. Historical coach-1.0 acceptance is not coach-2.0 acceptance. Read the dialogue first and record what the spoken words establish before interpreting the card. Exact cards are already in this invocation: label internal-dialogue-first, never blind or human review. Do not invent a charitable backstory; harmless unspecified names/history are not defects. Fill coach2 for ORIGINAL dialogue in writer output and CANDIDATE dialogue in reviewer output. Copy the supplied dialogue hash for the text being assessed. Give concise actual turn evidence, not generic claims.
G1: legible immediate situation, wants/stakes; separate stated, ordinary inferred, and missing essentials. Identify first material defect or explicitly none.
G2: coherent facts, ownership, timing, language, knowledge; recognizable misunderstanding/revelation is allowed, unstated intervening events are not.
G3: assess all A1-B2, B2-A3, A3-B4, B4-A5 links. Vocabulary repetition alone is insufficient. Purposeful avoidance must read as behavior.
G4: B is a plausible participant with an intelligible practical/emotional position, not a contrived punchline cue. B can help, concede or solve.
G5: exact card changes A's choices. For pairs Stance changes HOW A pursues Drive and B responds to the merged behavior; neither card may be decorative.
G6: ending develops the same behavior using B4. Investigate if A5 would work after unrelated B4; more obstacles are not required for heightening.
format: five spoken ABABA turns, existing word/schema limit, no narration/coaching/truncation.
Every mandatory gate and transition is PASS, FAIL or UNCLEAR with evidence; UNCLEAR cannot be accepted. All gates pass AND total >=85 AND fidelity/response >=4 AND others >=3; preserve the six weights 30/20/15/15/10/10. A 5 is not merely presence. Totals are derived in code. Retain good originals; no rewrite quota. Review both alternatives for different tactics, relationships or pressure. Scene outline identifies roles, task, A want, B want, stakes, exact-card tactic and B's contribution; it is private planning evidence, not a substitute for missing spoken facts. Humour must come from sincere priorities and responsive choices, not stock hierarchy or unrelated slogans. Record actual weaknesses and reservations. Writer corrections target only rejected/materially changed scenes; preserve all accepted records and prior original assessments exactly. No coach-1.0 failure or exhausted allowance is erased by this separately versioned cycle.

cards.title: The Only Professional
cards.instruction: Behave as the only qualified person present. Correct mistakes with patient, increasingly strained professionalism.

cards.title: Help Me Keep This Quiet
cards.instruction: Get someone to help contain a secret without first revealing its full risk or purpose.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Put this envelope in your coat pocket before Mum comes in. Flat, please; don't fold it.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Shall I tell her you asked me to take it home?

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: No. A handover isn't a family announcement. Just take your coat with you.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: She's coming in. She'll ask why I'm wearing it at the table.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Over your arm, then. With the pocket facing you. Let me do the talking.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Hold my spare cupboard key until tomorrow. Don't mention it to your flatmate.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I'll label it so she doesn't mistake it for ours.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: No label. Identifying a key for someone who mustn't know it's here defeats the arrangement. Keep it in your purse.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I'm lending her the purse tonight.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Then put it in your own coat. Check the pockets before you lend anyone anything else.

cards.title: The Only Professional
cards.instruction: Behave as the only qualified person present. Correct mistakes with patient, increasingly strained professionalism.

cards.title: Not Until You Explain
cards.instruction: Keep someone present until they account for one contradiction, omission, or suspicious change in their story.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Wait. You said you were at work until six. This taxi receipt says five. Let's get the times straight before you go.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: It was five when I left. That's my bus.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Then six wasn't leaving work. Was it getting home? One event per time, please. I'll drive you.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Six was when I reached the hotel. I wasn't ready to tell you.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Thank you. We're up to the hotel. Put your bag down and tell me why you went there.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Before I sign: our wedding invitation says Friday; your booking says Monday. Which document needs correcting?

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: The invitation. Monday saved a fortune. I've got to get to work.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: A changed booking needs a changed invitation. Stay here while we establish who has the wrong date.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Everyone. I thought we'd tell them after you signed.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Then the signature waits. Before we correct their invitations, explain why you thought signing could replace telling me.

cards.title: The Only Professional
cards.instruction: Behave as the only qualified person present. Correct mistakes with patient, increasingly strained professionalism.

cards.title: Apologize for the Lie
cards.instruction: Make someone acknowledge that the concealment or misdirection mattered, even if the underlying choice was defensible.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Cancelling the party was sensible. Not telling me wasn't. Start your apology with that distinction, please.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I didn't want to upset you.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: That explains the decision, not the effect. I turned up with a cake. What were you expecting me to do with it?

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I'm sorry you had to carry it all the way home.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Closer. Now include the part where you knew I was coming and let me.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: You gave me the rescue dog's photo and hid the page about chewing furniture. That's not a complete handover.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: You'd have said no. He needed a home.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Then you knew the missing page mattered. Please acknowledge that before we discuss where he sleeps.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I'll pay for any damage. Can we just settle him in?

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: We can. But 'I'll pay' is a budget, not an apology. Tell me you should have shown me the page.

cards.title: Approve the Cover Story
cards.instruction: Get someone to endorse an explanation that protects the plan, reputation, or people involved.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: If the caretaker asks, we were checking the props cupboard for extra seating. Can you stick to that?

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I'll tell him we borrowed his key to get the chairs.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Stools. Chairs don't fit. And don't volunteer the key before he's asked about it.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: He lent it to me. He'll expect me to say how we used it.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Then say you lent it on to me. I'll explain the seating check. Please don't improvise any furniture.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Approve 'storage problem' for the newsletter, please. Our volunteer delivered the cake on time; I'm not letting her take the blame.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Why not say we left it by the radiator?

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Because a report needs the failure, not a tour of the room. 'Stored too warmly.' Can you approve that?

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: With 'full refund'. They paid for a cake they couldn't eat.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Full refund promised or paid? Check before you sign. I'm trying to repair one mistake, not publish another.

cards.title: The Only Professional
cards.instruction: Behave as the only qualified person present. Correct mistakes with patient, increasingly strained professionalism.

cards.title: You Handle the Evidence
cards.instruction: Make someone else take responsibility for the evidence, loose end, or difficult follow-up.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Take this raffle cashbox and broken key to the treasurer. I'd rather you dealt with her questions.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I'll tape it shut and leave it on her desk.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: No unattended cash. Hand it to her and count it together. Write down the total before you discuss the lock.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: She'll ask how you snapped the key.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Say I turned it and it broke. No theories about force. Wait for her receipt, please.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Please get a replacement receipt from the magician. I paid him, but you've got his number.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I'll ask him to put yesterday's date on another one.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Ask for a duplicate of the original, not a new payment. The treasurer mustn't think we booked him twice.

beats.text: He only sends duplicates directly to the treasurer.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Then give her the number and explain what to ask for. Stay copied in; I need the receipt, not a successful introduction.
